children: Mobile payments group Airtel Money may list at up to $9 bln, ending a fallow period for the UK capital. That valuation reflects both rapid growth and high margins, making it exactly the kind of financial technology group the City would love to attract, but struggles to nurture.
Full view will be published shortly.
Follow Jennifer Johnson on Bluesky and LinkedIn.
Airtel Money, the mobile money arm of telecoms groups Airtel Africa, announced on September 23 that it plans to file for an initial public offering in London.

According to the Financial Times, the company is hoping to raise $800 million at a total valuation of $8 billion to $9 billion. The listing will be completed via a secondary offering of existing shares, leaving Airtel Money with a free float of at least 10%.
The company had originally aimed for ​a listing in the first half of 2026 but delayed it,⁠ citing unfavourable market conditions.
